title: Myth: == is just a looser ===
why_it_matters: Loose equality hides type conversions that break real logic.
explanation: Fact: == converts types before comparing, using rules that are hard to predict. === compares type and value with no conversion, so it does what it looks like it does. Default to === everywhere and you'll rarely get surprised.
code:
console.log(0 == "");   // true
console.log("1" == 1);  // true
console.log(0 === "");  // false
console.log("1" === 1); // false
try_it: Search your code for a double-equals comparison and change it to ===.
